record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Write Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for focus-focus singularities in Berezin-Toeplitz quantisation.

evidence.quote: Problem 7.3 (S. V. Ngo.c). Write Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for focus-focus singularities in Berezin-Toeplitz quantisation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega,J)$ be a prequantizable compact Kähler manifold with prequantum line bundle $(L,h)\to M$ whose Chern curvature equals $-i\omega$. For each positive integer $k$, let $\mathcal{H}_k=H^0(M,L^{\otimes k})$ be the space of holomorphic sections, equipped with the $L^2$-inner product induced by $h$ and the Liouville volume, and let $\Pi_k:L^2(M,L^{\otimes k})\to\mathcal{H}_k$ be the Szegő (Bergman) projector. For a smooth real-valued function $f\in C^\infty(M)$, the Berezin–Toeplitz operator at semiclassical parameter $\hbar=1/k$ is 
$$T_k(f)=\Pi_k\,M_f\,\Pi_k:\mathcal{H}_k\to\mathcal{H}_k,$$
where $M_f$ denotes multiplication by $f$.

Consider an integrable system of $n$ Poisson-commuting Hamiltonians $f_1,\dots,f_n\in C^\infty(M)$ generating a momentum map $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$, and assume that $m\in M$ is a non-degenerate critical point of focus-focus type, i.e., $n=2$ and there exist local symplectic coordinates $(x_1,y_1,x_2,y_2)$ around $m$ in which the Hessians of $f_1,f_2$ at $m$ span the focus-focus subalgebra generated by $q_1=x_1 y_1+x_2 y_2$ and $q_2=x_1 y_2-x_2 y_1$. The quantum integrable system is the commuting tuple $(T_k(f_1),T_k(f_2))$, and its joint spectrum is
$$\mathrm{JointSpec}(T_k(f_1),T_k(f_2))=\{(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2: \exists\,v\neq 0,\ T_k(f_j)v=\lambda_j v\}.$$

Problem. Derive Bohr–Sommerfeld quantization conditions describing, as $k\to\infty$ (equivalently $\hbar\to 0$), the joint eigenvalues of $(T_k(f_1),T_k(f_2))$ lying in any sufficiently small neighborhood of the critical value $F(m)\in\mathbb{R}^2$. The conditions should provide an explicit asymptotic characterization of the joint spectrum near the focus-focus value in terms of symplectic invariants of the singular Lagrangian fibration (such as the Taylor series invariant of the focus-focus singularity) together with subprincipal and curvature contributions intrinsic to Berezin–Toeplitz quantization.
artifact.status_search_result: Bohr–Sommerfeld-type conditions near focus-focus singularities have been developed in the pseudodifferential setting (e.g., Vũ Ngọc's singular Bohr-Sommerfeld rules), and recent work by Pelayo–Vũ Ngọc and collaborators on the inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems and on Berezin–Toeplitz Bohr–Sommerfeld rules has extended much of the framework to the Berezin–Toeplitz setting, assuming such rules hold. A fully explicit, all-orders Berezin–Toeplitz Bohr–Sommerfeld formula at focus-focus singularities does not appear to be fully established in the literature; the problem appears partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Semiclassical inverse spectral theory for singularities of focus-focus type
status_evidence.snippet: The joint spectrum near a focus-focus critical value determines the classical Lagrangian foliation, assuming the Bohr-Sommerfeld rules hold; applies to h-pseudodifferential operators and Berezin-Toeplitz operators on prequantizable compact symplectic manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Results in this direction assume rather than fully establish Berezin-Toeplitz Bohr-Sommerfeld rules at focus-focus singularities.

status_evidence.title: Regular Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for non-self-adjoint Berezin–Toeplitz operators
status_evidence.snippet: Develops Bohr–Sommerfeld conditions for Berezin–Toeplitz operators in the regular (non-singular) case.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress provides Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for regular Berezin–Toeplitz operators, but not specifically at focus-focus singularities.

status_evidence.title: The inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit formulas recover symplectic invariants of classical semitoric systems from semiclassical asymptotics of joint spectra of Berezin–Toeplitz quantum semitoric systems.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on extracting focus-focus invariants from Berezin–Toeplitz joint spectra has been made.
